title: LQ13 — Design an LRU / LFU Cache
relevance: High — the bridge LLD + DSA design problem (coding screens + OOD rounds); Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Uber, Flipkart, Atlassian, and most product cos probe HashMap+DLL composition, Strategy for eviction, and concurrency.
company_notes: Very common across campus coding and LLD/machine-coding rounds: LRU is treated as mandatory, LFU is a common stronger follow-up, and experienced loops add TTL, concurrency, stats, and production cache discussion (Redis/Caffeine/TinyLFU).

phases.goal: Lock down exact cache semantics and non-functional constraints before design.

must_hit.point: States mandatory behavior: fixed capacity, get(key), put(key,value), and eviction on overflow by the chosen policy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “I’ll confirm fixed capacity and define get/put behavior plus eviction when capacity is full.”

must_hit.point: Commits to O(1) average for both get and put as the primary contract.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “The target is O(1) average for both operations, so structure choice must enforce that.”

must_hit.point: Clarifies policy semantics: get counts as use, and LFU tie-break is LRU within the same frequency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “On read we update recency/frequency, and LFU ties evict the least recently used in that bucket.”

probes: What assumptions do you want to confirm before coding this cache?

hints.1: List the minimal functional API and when eviction happens.
hints.2: Add performance and policy semantics, especially what get should update.
hints.3: State fixed capacity + O(1) get/put + get updates usage + LFU ties by LRU.

phases.goal: Identify the minimal state objects and invariants needed for O(1) operations.

must_hit.point: For LRU, uses Map<K, Node> plus one doubly linked list with sentinel head/tail (MRU at head, LRU at tail).
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Map gives key lookup; DLL gives O(1) recency reorder and tail eviction.”

must_hit.point: For LFU, uses keyToNode, freqToList, and minFreq to locate eviction bucket in O(1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: “I keep a map from key to node, a map from frequency to DLL, and track minFreq.”

must_hit.point: Node stores key as well as value and links so eviction can delete from map in O(1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Node must carry key; otherwise eviction cannot remove map entry directly.”

probes: Which core data structures do you need for LRU and LFU, and why?

hints.1: A single structure cannot satisfy fast lookup and fast eviction updates together.
hints.2: Pair hash lookup with linked ordering; LFU needs per-frequency ordering.
hints.3: Use map + DLL for LRU, and keyToNode + freqToList + minFreq for LFU.

phases.goal: Define clean responsibilities and interfaces so policy and storage concerns stay decoupled.

must_hit.point: Defines cache-facing API (get, put) and positions optional invalidate/clear/stats as extensions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “I’ll keep a small cache API first, then add invalidate/clear/stats if requested.”

must_hit.point: Separates responsibilities: Cache coordinates, DoublyLinkedList handles pointer surgery, policy decides victim.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Cache should not do raw pointer manipulation; list helpers own remove/addFront/removeLast.”

must_hit.point: Uses EvictionPolicy Strategy boundary to avoid policy if/else soup and support LRU/LFU swapping.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Cache depends on an EvictionPolicy interface so policy changes do not rewrite callers.”

probes: How would you split classes so this stays extensible and testable?

hints.1: Start from API facade vs internal helpers.
hints.2: Isolate list pointer operations and eviction decision logic.
hints.3: Cache facade + DLL utility + policy interface is the clean split.

phases.goal: Show correct update/eviction flows that preserve invariants on every get/put path.

must_hit.point: LRU hit path unlinks the node and moves it to head on get and on put update.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Any access/update refreshes recency: remove node then addFront.”

must_hit.point: LRU overflow evicts tail.prev and removes the same key from map in the same operation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Victim is list tail predecessor; evict from list and map together.”

must_hit.point: LFU access removes from current frequency list, increments frequency, re-inserts into new list, and bumps minFreq when the old min bucket becomes empty.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “On access I migrate node to freq+1 list and advance minFreq if prior list emptied.”

must_hit.point: LFU new insert starts at frequency 1 with minFreq = 1, and eviction removes LRU tail from the minFreq list.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Fresh keys start in freq 1; victim is tail of current minFreq bucket.”

probes: Walk me through put when capacity is full for both LRU and LFU.
What exact state changes happen on a get hit?

hints.1: Trace one hit and one overflow path with list and map updates.
hints.2: Name the victim location for each policy before coding.
hints.3: LRU evicts tail.prev; LFU evicts tail of minFreq list after promotion bookkeeping.

phases.goal: Demonstrate policy and feature evolution without rewriting core cache callers.

must_hit.point: Applies Strategy so new eviction policies can be added without changing cache clients (OCP signal).
must_hit.evidence_hint: “I can plug LRU or LFU (and future policies) behind the same cache interface.”

must_hit.point: Treats TTL as orthogonal to capacity eviction: store expiresAt, lazily expire on get, and optionally sweep in background.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “TTL expiry is separate from LRU/LFU choice; expired entries are misses and removed.”

must_hit.point: Positions Factory, Proxy/Decorator, and Observer for creation, data-store wrapping, and eviction/stats notifications.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Factory picks policy, caching proxy fronts store, observer hooks power removal/stats events.”

probes: If tomorrow we need another policy and TTL, what changes and what stays stable?

hints.1: Separate policy choice from cache API surface.
hints.2: Keep expiry logic independent from capacity policy logic.
hints.3: Use EvictionPolicy strategy plus optional factory/proxy/observer hooks.

phases.goal: Establish correctness under concurrent access and discuss throughput scaling choices.

must_hit.point: Starts with one lock around get/put mutations across map and ordering structures as the safe baseline.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “I’ll first guarantee correctness with a single lock guarding map+list state changes.”

must_hit.point: Explains that get is not a pure read for LRU/LFU because it mutates order/frequency, so naive read-lock assumptions are unsafe.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Even get mutates internals, so read/write split needs care.”

must_hit.point: Mentions scaling options: striped or segmented caches via hash(key) % N to reduce contention.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “To improve throughput, shard into independent segments and lock per segment.”

must_hit.point: Avoids holding lock during slow loads; uses load outside lock then put (or singleflight) to keep critical section small.
must_hit.evidence_hint: “Never keep global lock while calling a slow loader; compute outside, then insert safely.”

probes: How would you make this thread-safe first, then scale throughput if contention is high?

hints.2: Identify every path that mutates map/list state, including get.
hints.3: Use one lock baseline, then discuss striping/segmentation and short critical sections.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: LinkedHashMap (access-order + removeEldestEntry) is a fast Java-only LRU shortcut, but hand-rolled map+DLL better demonstrates O(1) mechanics and extends cleanly to LFU, portability, and custom concurrency.
Separate classes are simpler for single-policy coding prompts, while EvictionPolicy Strategy is preferable when the requirement is to support both or switch policy at construction.
A single synchronized/reentrant lock is the safest interview baseline; striped segments improve throughput under contention but increase design complexity and require careful invariants.

tradeoffs.topic: Exact LFU vs approximate LFU/LRU in production
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Interview solutions usually expect exact O(1) LFU structures; production systems often use sampled or sketch-based approaches (for example TinyLFU-style ideas) to balance memory and CPU.

gotchas.trap: Treating get as read-only and not updating recency/frequency.
gotchas.correction: For both LRU and LFU, get must count as use and update ordering/frequency state.

gotchas.trap: Evicting arbitrary key when LFU frequencies tie.
gotchas.correction: Within the same frequency bucket, evict the least recently used node (bucket tail).

gotchas.trap: Evicting when updating an existing key at full capacity.
gotchas.correction: Update value and usage metadata in place; size is unchanged so no eviction.

gotchas.trap: Not handling capacity 0 and capacity 1 edge behavior.
gotchas.correction: Define and implement explicit behavior for capacity 0 and validate thrash behavior for capacity 1.

gotchas.trap: Node does not store key, making map cleanup expensive on eviction.
gotchas.correction: Store key inside node so eviction removes both list node and map entry in O(1).

gotchas.trap: LFU minFreq not updated after promotions or empty-bucket cleanup.
gotchas.correction: When a frequency list empties, remove it and advance minFreq when appropriate.

gotchas.trap: Using a heap for LFU while still claiming O(1) operations.
gotchas.correction: A heap makes access updates O(log n); use freq-to-DLL buckets for O(1) interview target.
